headline: Highest risk is medium: CrewAI can write and browse while Superset exposes an API, creating default-path prompt, data, and workflow coupling without documented isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and parse stdin/stdout, while Superset exposes a Superset API and allowlisted egress. If CrewAI ingests Superset-generated content from shared files or API responses as instructions, prompt injection is plausible in default setups. The pair lacks documented isolation, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF CrewAI reads Superset-produced files or API responses as trusted instructions
IF both agents share a writable workspace without provenance tagging
mitigations: Separate workspaces for each agent
Add provenance labels to all inter-agent files
Disable automatic instruction-following on imported text
Require human review before CrewAI acts on Superset output

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, and can write/read the host filesystem; Superset exposes an API and has allowlisted egress. If sensitive crew data is placed in shared files or passed through Superset workflows, leakage can occur in default configurations. No evidence shows PHI or secrets in Superset, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF developer-passed crew data includes secrets or regulated data
IF Superset API outputs are stored in the same directory CrewAI reads
mitigations: Keep sensitive inputs out of shared directories
Use separate service accounts and API credentials
Redact secrets before passing data between agents
Restrict Superset API responses to non-sensitive fields

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI has unrestricted filesystem write and subprocess execution, while Superset can call its API and has allowlisted network egress. Their capabilities overlap on mutable resources if they share a workspace or API-backed state, creating race and overwrite risk. Because no locking or coordination is documented, the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or config files
IF both agents mutate the same Superset-backed resource without locks
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Use read-only access for one agent
Snapshot shared state before each run

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI can generate outputs from crew memory and tools, and Superset can consume API data for analytics. If Superset treats CrewAI output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into dashboards or downstream actions. The pair does not document a verification boundary, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Superset ingests CrewAI-produced text or metrics without validation
IF CrewAI output is used as a source of truth for reports or alerts
mitigations: Add schema validation before ingestion
Require a second source for critical metrics
Mark CrewAI outputs as untrusted by default
Review dashboard changes before publishing

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI explicitly handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, while Superset’s profile shows no handled secrets or regulated data classes. The profiles do not indicate a residency or certification mismatch, so only a small compliance gap is visible. I do not cite Superset data classes because none are listed.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into CrewAI workflows
IF Superset is configured to store or export that same regulated data
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in CrewAI crews
Document retention settings for both systems
Confirm export/delete workflows before use
Keep audit logs for data transfers
